name: Ginisang Sayote
description: Tender sayote sautéed with garlic, onion and tomato in just a touch of oil.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula. Use a non-stick pan with a lid.
Rinse all vegetables under running water. Peel or trim as needed: remove the seeds of sayote or ampalaya, peel upo, patola and kalabasa, and cut off the tough ends of pechay, kangkong and sitaw.
Cut the main vegetables into bite-size pieces, about 2 cm (the width of your thumb). Keep the pieces the same size so they cook evenly.
Mince the garlic (chop into tiny bits), slice the onion thinly and chop the tomato. Put them in a small bowl. Measure the water and salt.
Put the pan on the stove over medium heat. After 1 minute, add the {oil} of oil. It is ready when a piece of onion sizzles gently.

Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Do not let it turn dark brown, because it turns bitter. Add the onion and stir for 1 minute until soft. Add the tomato and press it with the spatula for 1–2 minutes until mushy.
Add the main vegetables and stir for 1 minute so they are coated. Pour in {water} of water.
Cover the pan, turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 8–10 minutes. Stir once halfway. It is done when a fork goes in easily but the pieces still hold their shape.
Sprinkle in the salt and a little black pepper. Stir and taste. If it needs more flavor, add a squeeze of calamansi instead of more salt.
Turn off the heat and serve warm with rice. Keep leftovers in a covered container in the fridge for up to 2 days.

name: Tortang Talong
description: Smoky charred eggplant in a fluffy egg coating, pan-cooked with a little oil.
instructions: Wash your hands and clean your work area.
Rinse the eggplant. Poke it 3–4 times with a fork so it does not burst. Do not cut off the stem.

Cook the eggplant until soft: over a gas flame with tongs, turning every 2 minutes for 8–10 minutes; or on a tray in a 200°C oven for 20–25 minutes. It is done when the skin is wrinkled and it feels very soft.
Let it cool for 5 minutes. Peel off the skin gently, holding the stem. Flatten the flesh with a fork on a plate.
Crack the egg into a shallow bowl. Add the chopped onion and the salt and beat with a fork until well mixed.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Brush with {oil} of oil (or use an air fryer at 180°C for the cooking step).
Dip the eggplant in the egg on both sides. Place it in the pan and cook 2–3 minutes until golden. Flip carefully with a wide spatula and cook 2 more minutes.
Serve warm with sliced fresh tomato and rice.

instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula. Use a separate cutting board for raw chicken or fish, or wash the board and knife with hot soapy water right after. Wash your hands too.

description: Ginger-scented chicken soup with sayote and malunggay.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula.

Mince the garlic, slice the onion and ginger thinly.
Put a pot over medium heat. After 1 minute add the {oil} of oil. Add the garlic, ginger and onion and stir for 2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula.

Rinse all the ingredients. Peel and cut the vegetables into bite-size pieces. If using chicken, cut it into 2 cm pieces (see the tip about a separate cutting board and washing your hands after touching raw chicken).
Mince the garlic, slice the onion and ginger thinly.
Put a pot over medium heat. After 1 minute add the {oil} of oil. Add the garlic, ginger and onion and stir for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken (or beans) and stir for 3–4 minutes.
Pour in {water} of water and bring to a boil (big bubbles). If foam appears on top, scoop it off with a spoon.
Lower the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15–20 minutes until the chicken has no pink inside and the harder vegetables are soft.
Add the leafy greens and any tomato. Cook for 2 more minutes, no longer, so the greens stay green.
Add the salt. Taste and adjust with black pepper or a little calamansi.
Serve hot in a bowl with rice.

name: Vegetable Soup
description: A light, comforting soup of potato, chayote, carrots and cabbage.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula.
Peel the potato, sayote and carrots. Cut them into 2 cm cubes. Shred the cabbage and slice the celery.
Mince the garlic and slice the onion.
Put a pot over medium heat with the {oil} of oil. Cook the garlic and onion for 1 minute.
Add the potato, sayote, carrots and {water} of water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover and simmer 12 minutes.
Add the cabbage and celery and cook 5 more minutes. Check that the potato is soft with a fork.
Add the salt and pepper, taste, and serve hot.

name: Ginataang Kalabasa at Sitaw
description: Sweet kalabasa and sitaw in a light coconut sauce, with no frying at all.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula.
Peel the kalabasa, remove the seeds, and cut into 3 cm cubes. Trim the ends of the sitaw and cut into 5 cm lengths.
Mince the garlic and ginger and slice the onion.
In a pot over medium heat, add the garlic, ginger, onion and {water} of water. Bring to a boil.
Add the kalabasa, cover, and simmer 6 minutes until it starts to soften.
Add the sitaw and the light coconut milk. Lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 5 more minutes. Do not boil hard, because coconut milk can separate.
Season with the salt, taste, and serve warm with rice.

name: Sinigang na Gulay (fresh, no mix)
description: Sour vegetable soup soured with fresh calamansi instead of salty sinigang mix.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula.

Peel the labanos and cut into rounds. Cut the eggplant into thick slices, the sitaw into 5 cm lengths and the kangkong into 5 cm pieces (leaves and stems separate). Quarter the tomato and slice the onion.
In a pot combine {water} of water, the tomato and onion. Bring to a boil and simmer 5 minutes until the tomato is soft.
Add the labanos and the whole siling haba. Cook 5 minutes.
Add the eggplant and sitaw. Cook 4 more minutes.
Add the kangkong stems, then the leaves 1 minute later. Turn off the heat.
Stir in the calamansi juice and the salt. Taste: it should be pleasantly sour. Add a bit more calamansi if you want. Serve hot.

name: Light Chopsuey
description: Colorful mixed vegetables with a little chicken, stir-fried in very little oil.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula. Use a separate cutting board for raw chicken or fish, or wash the board and knife with hot soapy water right after. Wash your hands too.
Rinse the vegetables. Cut them into thin, bite-size pieces about the same size. Cut the chicken into thin strips 1 cm wide.
Mince the garlic and slice the onion. Put the chicken, vegetables and aromatics in separate small bowls so they are ready to add. Stir-frying goes fast.
Heat a wide pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add the {oil} of oil.
Add the garlic and onion and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and stir for 3–4 minutes until no pink is left.

Add the hard vegetables first (carrots, cauliflower, broccoli) and stir for 2 minutes. Add the softer ones (cabbage, peppers, beans) and stir 2 more minutes. Pour in {water} of water and cover for 2 minutes.
Add the low-sodium soy sauce or salt, plus pepper. Toss well and taste. The vegetables should be tender but still slightly crisp.
Serve right away with rice.

name: Baked Salmon with Vegetables
description: Salmon baked on a tray with broccoli and carrots, lemon and pepper.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula. Use a separate cutting board for raw chicken or fish, or wash the board and knife with hot soapy water right after. Wash your hands too.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Cut the vegetables into thin bite-size pieces so they cook as fast as the fish. Pat the fish dry with a paper towel.
Place the vegetables on one side of the tray and the fish on the other. Drizzle with {oil} of oil and lemon or calamansi juice. Sprinkle with the salt and pepper.
Bake for 15–18 minutes. The fish is done when it flakes easily and looks white all the way through. The vegetables should be soft.
Use oven mitts to take out the tray. Serve warm with rice.

name: Steamed Chicken with Kalabasa
description: Soft, juicy steamed chicken over sweet kalabasa with ginger.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula. Use a separate cutting board for raw chicken or fish, or wash the board and knife with hot soapy water right after. Wash your hands too.
Slice the ginger into thin strips, slice the onion and cut the vegetables into thin bite-size pieces so they cook fast.
Set up a steamer. No steamer? Pour 3 cm of water into a wide pot, put a small heatproof bowl upside down in the middle, and set a heatproof plate on top of the bowl.
Bring the water to a boil.
Put the fish, chicken or tofu on the plate and scatter the ginger, onion and vegetables on top. Drizzle with the {oil} of oil, the calamansi juice (if any) and the salt.
Cover the pot. Steam over medium heat: 10–12 minutes for fish, 15–18 minutes for sliced chicken, 8 minutes for tofu. Add hot water to the pot if it gets low.
It is done when the fish flakes easily, or the thickest chicken piece has no pink inside. Ask an adult if you are unsure, or cut into the thickest part to check.
Turn off the heat. Carefully lift the lid away from your face because the steam is very hot. Use oven mitts to remove the plate.
Serve hot with the juices from the plate and rice.

name: Ginisang Kamatis with Itlog
description: Soft scrambled egg cooked in juicy sautéed tomato and onion.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula.
Rinse the tomato and chop it into small cubes. Slice the onion thinly and mince the garlic. Slice the green onion, if any.
Crack the egg into a bowl, add the salt, and beat with a fork for about 20 seconds until no clear egg white is left.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add the {oil} of oil. Cook the garlic and onion for 1 minute.
Add the tomato and cook 3–4 minutes, pressing it until it turns into a soft sauce.
Lower the heat to low. Pour in the egg and wait 20 seconds. Gently push the egg from the edges to the middle with a spatula and repeat until soft curds form, about 1–2 minutes.
Turn off the heat while the egg still looks slightly wet; it keeps cooking in the pan. Top with green onion and serve with rice.

name: Creamy Kalabasa Soup
description: A warm, naturally creamy soup made just from kalabasa, onion and garlic.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula.
Peel the kalabasa, remove the seeds, and cut into 2 cm cubes. Slice the onion and mince the garlic.
Put a pot over medium heat with the {oil} of oil. Cook the onion and garlic for 2 minutes.
Add the kalabasa and {water} of water. Bring to a boil, cover, then simmer 15 minutes until it is very soft.
Turn off the heat. Mash the kalabasa in the pot with a potato masher or fork until mostly smooth. (Or blend carefully in a blender in small batches.)
Return to low heat for 2 minutes. Add the salt and pepper, taste, and serve warm.

name: Ginisang Sitaw at Kamatis
description: Crisp sitaw sautéed with tomato, garlic and onion.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula. Use a non-stick pan with a lid.
Rinse all vegetables under running water. Peel or trim as needed: remove the seeds of sayote or ampalaya, peel upo, patola and kalabasa, and cut off the tough ends of pechay, kangkong and sitaw.
Cut the main vegetables into bite-size pieces, about 2 cm (the width of your thumb). Keep the pieces the same size so they cook evenly.
Mince the garlic (chop into tiny bits), slice the onion thinly and chop the tomato. Put them in a small bowl. Measure the water and salt.
Put the pan on the stove over medium heat. After 1 minute, add the {oil} of oil. It is ready when a piece of onion sizzles gently.

Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Do not let it turn dark brown, because it turns bitter. Add the onion and stir for 1 minute until soft. Add the tomato and press it with the spatula for 1–2 minutes until mushy.
Add the main vegetables and stir for 1 minute so they are coated. Pour in {water} of water.
Cover the pan, turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 8–10 minutes. Stir once halfway. It is done when a fork goes in easily but the pieces still hold their shape.
Sprinkle in the salt and a little black pepper. Stir and taste. If it needs more flavor, add a squeeze of calamansi instead of more salt.
Turn off the heat and serve warm with rice. Keep leftovers in a covered container in the fridge for up to 2 days.

name: Light Chicken Sopas
description: Comforting macaroni soup with chicken and vegetables, without processed ingredients.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and clean your work area. Get out a cutting board, a sharp knife, measuring spoons and a spatula.
Use a separate cutting board for raw chicken or fish, or wash the board and knife with hot soapy water right after. Wash your hands too.
Cut the chicken into small 1 cm pieces. Dice the carrots and celery, shred the cabbage, mince the garlic and slice the onion.
In a pot over medium heat add the {oil} of oil and cook the garlic and onion for 1 minute. Add the chicken and stir for 3–4 minutes until no pink is left.
Add {water} of water and bring to a boil. Add the carrots and celery and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the macaroni and stir well so it does not stick. Cook 8 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the cabbage and cook 2 more minutes. Add the salt and pepper, taste and serve hot.
